name: Cozumel
tagline: World-Class Diving and Island Life at Mexican Prices
description: Cozumel is a laid-back Caribbean island off the Yucatan coast, famous for its world-class coral reefs and crystal-clear waters. Unlike the party scene of nearby Cancun, Cozumel maintains a relaxed, small-town feel with a genuine Mexican community alongside a friendly expat population. The cost of living is remarkably low for a Caribbean island, thanks to Mexican pricing on everything from healthcare to tacos. If you love diving, snorkeling, or simply living on island time, Cozumel is hard to beat.

quickFacts.visa: Tourist visa 180 days; Temporary Resident visa (1-4 years) available
quickFacts.language: Spanish, English widely spoken in tourist areas
quickFacts.safetyRating: High – one of Mexico's safest destinations

housing.description: Basic studio or rented room in an inland local colonia (Colonia Independencia, Emiliano Zapata), off the malecón

dining.description: Taquerías and the Mercado Municipal a few times a week; mostly home cooking

healthcare.description: Basic Mexico-only private major-medical (GNP/AXA Mexico) or IMSS voluntary; on-island clinic with a ferry to Playa del Carmen for specialists. Assumes an early retiree (45–55); older retirees should budget more

transportation.description: Bicycle and colectivos plus the occasional taxi; no car (Cozumel has no Uber)

entertainment.description: Free public beaches, cheap cantinas, sunset walks on the malecón

1M.lifestyle: A basic studio or rented room in an inland colonia keeps housing low, away from the tourist-priced malecón. Meals come mostly from the Mercado Municipal, with cheap taquería plates a few times a week, and a bicycle plus shared colectivos handle getting around — Cozumel has no Uber, so the taxi is an occasional splurge. Health cover is a basic Mexico-only private plan, using the island's clinic for routine needs and a short ferry to Playa del Carmen for specialists. The reef and the beaches are effectively free, which is the whole point; the budget is tight but the setting is not.

housing.description: Furnished 1BR on the edge of the centre or in a modest condo development

dining.description: Out two or three times a week, mixing local eateries with tourist-district spots like Kinta and Kondesa

healthcare.description: Comprehensive Mexico-only private plan (GNP/AXA/MetLife Mexico) with access to Cancún's hospitals

transportation.description: An owned scooter or golf cart plus taxis; ferry trips to the mainland

entertainment.description: Beach clubs, regular diving, and a social calendar

2M.lifestyle: A furnished 1BR near the centre or in a modest condo development steps up the comfort without leaving the island's easy rhythm. Dining out becomes a two-or-three-times-a-week habit across local eateries and tourist-district favorites, and a scooter or golf cart replaces the bicycle. Comprehensive Mexico-only private insurance opens up Cancún's better hospitals, a short flight or ferry away. Regular diving on the Mesoamerican reef, beach clubs, and an active social scene fill the weeks — comfortable island living at Mexican prices.

housing.description: Quality furnished 1BR or small condo in a good location near the malecón or a development like Las Fincas or Coral Princess

dining.description: Out around four times a week, including the island's better restaurants — Kondesa, Buccanos, Guido's, La Cocay

healthcare.description: Comprehensive local cover with a medevac rider or entry-level international plan (evacuation to the mainland)

transportation.description: Owned golf cart or scooter plus taxis and frequent ferry trips to the mainland

entertainment.description: Regular scuba diving — Cozumel's world-class signature — plus beach clubs and boating

3M.lifestyle: A quality furnished 1BR or small condo in a desirable pocket near the water anchors a comfortable, unhurried island life. Dining out several times a week across Cozumel's better tables becomes routine, and diving the world-class reef shifts from a splurge to a standing habit. Health cover adds a medevac rider or an entry-level international plan, reflecting that serious specialists are a ferry or flight away. There is genuine margin at this level — the island's day-to-day costs are low enough that the budget stretches to frequent mainland trips and easy discretionary spending.

housing.description: Near-beach or oceanfront luxury condo (Peninsula Grand, El Cantil, Casa del Mar tier)

dining.description: Near-daily dining across the island's best restaurants and resort and beach-club venues

healthcare.description: International plan with medical evacuation to Houston or Miami

transportation.description: Owned car plus a golf cart and taxis; occasional boat fuel

entertainment.description: Frequent private dive and boat charters, deep-sea fishing, beach clubs

domesticHelp.description: Part-time housekeeper two or three days a week

luxuryExtras.description: Off-island travel, spa and wellness, dive- and yacht-club memberships

5M.lifestyle: An oceanfront or near-beach luxury condo puts the reef at the doorstep, with a part-time housekeeper handling the home a few days a week. Dining is near-daily across the island's best restaurants and resort venues, and the water-based luxury Cozumel does best — private dive and boat charters, deep-sea fishing — is on tap. An international plan with medical evacuation to Houston or Miami covers the gap left by the island's limited specialist care. This budget comfortably exceeds what the small island absorbs day to day, so the surplus flows into off-island travel, memberships, and wellness.

housing.description: Top beachfront villa or oceanfront penthouse, near the ceiling of the island's long-term luxury stock

dining.description: Near-daily fine dining across Cozumel's handful of genuinely upscale restaurants and resort tables

healthcare.description: Concierge international plan with worldwide coverage including the US and medevac to Houston or Miami

transportation.description: Car, golf cart, and a private dive or fishing boat, plus frequent flights off-island

entertainment.description: Private dive, fishing, and boat charters, beach clubs, and entertaining — the island over-delivers on water luxury

domesticHelp.description: Full-time housekeeper, cook, and caretaker for the property

luxuryExtras.description: Frequent luxury travel off-island, yacht- and dive-club memberships, wellness, and gear

10M.lifestyle: The top of what the island can support: a beachfront villa or oceanfront penthouse near the ceiling of Cozumel's long-term luxury stock, kept by a full-time housekeeper, cook, and caretaker. A private boat joins the car and golf cart, and the water luxuries the island genuinely over-delivers — chartered dives, deep-sea fishing, boating — are effectively unlimited. Concierge international cover with worldwide access and evacuation removes the island's one real weakness, distance from major hospitals. Fine dining is near-daily across Cozumel's handful of upscale rooms, and because the island's restaurant and retail luxury is finite, much of the discretionary budget flows into travel and charters rather than local spend.
